en: The Philippines has 7,641 islands, which is 534 more islands than its previous official count of 7,107.
Mount Apo is the highest peak in the Philippines at 2,954 meters, making it taller than Mount Pulag's 2,928 meters.
Mayon Volcano erupted over 50 times in the past 400 years, more than any other active volcano in the Philippines.
At 505 kilometers long, the Cagayan River is the longest in the Philippines, significantly longer than the 372-kilometer Rio Grande de Mindanao.
Covering 911 square kilometers, Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, much bigger than Lake Lanao's 388 square kilometers.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares, protecting over 600 fish species and 360 coral species in the Sulu Sea.
Baguio City receives around 3,800 millimeters of rain annually, which is roughly three times the average annual rainfall of Manila.
The Philippine Sea covers about 5.7 million square kilometers, which is roughly 19 times larger than the entire land area of the Philippines.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer underground river, which is one of the longest navigable underground rivers in the world.
Palawan is the largest Philippine province at 14,649 square kilometers, which is more than three times larger than the province of Cebu.
Luzon is the largest Philippine island at 109,965 square kilometers, which is about 22 times larger than the island of Bohol.
Tinuy-an Falls in Bislig City spans 55 meters wide and drops 26 meters, making it one of the widest waterfalls in Mindanao.
